newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Israel pressures Argentine court on 1992 bombing.
newsitem.headline: Israel pressures Argentine court on 1992 bombing.

text.p: Israel piled pressure on Argentina's Supreme Court on Monday to hand over to a federal judge the investigation into a 1992 bomb attack on its embassy in Buenos Aires that killed 29 people.

Frustration in Israel and in Argentina's Jewish community, one of the largest in the world, is reaching fever pitch over the lack of progress in investigations into the embassy bombing and another anti-Jewish attack in 1994 that killed 86 people.

Last Friday about 10,000 people took to the streets of Buenos Aires on the third anniversary of the 1994 bomb attack on the AMIA Jewish community centre in a show of bitterness and anger against the Argentine government, police and courts.

Not one person is under arrest for the embassy bombing. The 1994 attack, on the other hand, does not involve a foreign power and is thus being investigated by a federal judge, who has charged four policemen with providing the vehicle used.

Israeli Ambassador Yitzhak Aviran met President Carlos Menem on Monday to discuss the bombings. He told reporters later he would like the Supreme Court to delegate the embassy case and to pin the blame squarely on Iran and the armed Moslem group Hizbollah, whom Israel has blamed all along.
Israel and Argentine Jews have reacted with indignation to two Supreme Court judges espousing the theory that the embassy bomb was put inside the building by a Jewish extremist group.

"We hope for a firm decision from the Supreme Court to delegate the case to a judge, and to confirm this was an explosion directed by a spiritual or ideological 'father' that was Iran and executed by the international terrorists Hizbollah," said the diplomat.

Aviran accused the Supreme Court of "shelving the case for three years" and of "losing time" on the theory of a bomb from within. He urged the embassy case be delegated to Federal Judge Juan Jose Galeano, whose handling of the AMIA investigation has made better headway.
Opposition and government figures including Justice Minister Raul Granillo Ocampo have said they would favour Galeano handling both sensitive cases.
The diplomat said Menem's good relations with Israel were "clouded" by the bomb attacks and there was no guarantee that last Friday's bitter protests would not be repeated.

Crowds at Friday's ceremonies outside the rebuilt AMIA centre insulted Interior Minister Carlos Corach and Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez. Mourning relative Laura Ginsberg made a speech accusing Menem, by name, "of being the accomplice."
Menem summoned Jewish leader Ruben Beraja to express his displeasure. His ministers were still on the defensive Monday, with Corach saying, "Our consciences are absolutely clear."
